text: Particularly regarding a momentary object that has since ceased to exist, such as its form, taste, and so on. [The argument is that] since that which has not been experienced cannot be remembered by the mental consciousness, there must necessarily have been an experience of the object, and that experience is perception. However, the view that the form etc. of such an object is perceived is unproven, because this is [merely] the remembering of an object that was previously experienced.
